body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. The story leading the day is a deadly shooting at a Mojave store on Highway 58, where deputies found a man unresponsive and locked the business down while they sorted out what happened. Closer to home, a transit bus went off the road in southeast Bakersfield with six passengers hurt, and an east Bakersfield apartment fire displaced five people. Look for a high near 71 today under a flood watch that runs through Thursday evening, with air quality sitting at a moderate 59.

## The Kern Overnight

Gunfire made for the worst of the night. Deputies were called to a store on Highway 58 in Mojave just after 1 a.m. and found a man on the ground who was unresponsive; an ambulance was summoned and the store was locked down while investigators worked. Witnesses described a burgundy car with a disabled plate pulling out of the lot, driven by a light-skinned man with long hair, and callers reported two people running from the store toward the apartments behind it. One person detained at the scene said he saw the car leave.

Elsewhere, a single gunshot brought deputies to 22nd Street in central Bakersfield and turned up nothing behind it. Officers were sent to a bar where a man with a knife in his pocket was threatening a customer, and to an apartment complex where a man who threatened a resident and a roommate left with a handgun in a black backpack. A thief assaulted a worker who confronted him on South Union Avenue, and someone reported three or four people walking around with a shotgun.

Fire filled the rest of the night. A rig burned on the Brundage bridge, and a transit bus went off the road at Belle Terrace and South Washington in southeast Bakersfield just before 8 p.m., with six passengers reporting pain and dispatchers calling a third ambulance. Multiple callers reported fire in an east Bakersfield apartment on Monterey Street a little after 3 a.m., and the Red Cross was brought in for three women and two men who were displaced. A reinforced response went to a house on Angela Way in the Station 8 area before 5 a.m., where crews found the house charged with smoke on the east side and fire showing at a rear corner, knocked down a contents fire in the garage and secured the gas and electric. A grass fire on Elk Hills Road just before midnight drew two dozers, a water tender and several patrols, with crews routed in through oil field gates that the company opened for them.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 71 degrees and a low around 54 tonight. It's currently 59 at Meadows Field. The National Weather Service in Hanford has issued a flood watch that took effect at 5:04 this morning and runs until 8 p.m. Thursday, so keep an eye on low-lying roads and crossings if you're out and about. Air quality is 59, which registers as moderate — fine for most of us, but sensitive folks may want to take it easy on extended outdoor exertion. No active fires were reported in the region as of this morning.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that a new poll shows Xavier Becerra with a wide lead over Steve Hilton in the California governor race.** The survey puts the Democratic candidate well ahead of his Republican rival as the campaign moves deeper into the fall. For Kern County, the governor's race matters in concrete ways — water policy, oil and agriculture regulation, and the state funding that flows into local schools and roads all get shaped by whoever takes the office. We'll be watching whether the numbers hold as more voters tune in.

**According to 23ABC, tens of thousands of California state workers are expected to walk off the job Wednesday in a one-day strike that could affect services at the DMV, unemployment offices and other state agencies.** Members of SEIU Local 1000 are protesting what they call bad-faith bargaining by Gov. Gavin Newsom's administration; the union has been negotiating a new labor agreement since its three-year contract expired June 30, and this would be Local 1000's first statewide walkout in its 44-year history. The union represents about 100,000 public workers across dozens of agencies, and roughly 5,000 are legally excluded from participating because their absence would pose an imminent threat to public health or safety. DMV services could be delayed and some offices could close early, with possible effects at EDD, CalFresh and state parks. Union President Anica Walls urged Californians to "give our employees some grace," suggesting anyone who finds limited service at the DMV make an appointment for another day. The Public Employment Relations Board sided with the union last month, concluding that CalHR refused to meet and confer in good faith, while CalHR says departments have contingency plans for potential disruptions. The union could still call the strike off, and both sides are scheduled to keep talking.

**Bakersfield Now reports that the Tulare County Sheriff's Office is searching for four men accused of robbing a truck stop in Delano and stealing the register.** Deputies are asking for the public's help identifying the group. Truck stops along the 99 corridor are busy, cash-handling operations, and robberies there put late-night workers and travelers at risk — a reminder to keep an eye out and report anything that looks off.

**23ABC tells us that newly sworn-in U.S. Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling visited Kern County on Tuesday, touring agricultural and logistics operations and sitting down for a one-on-one interview after a roundtable at Grimmway Farms in Arvin.** Sonderling made two stops here — the Wonderful Logistics Center in Shafter in the morning and Grimmway in the afternoon — and said he came to hear employers' workforce challenges and find ways to draw more people into agriculture careers. A key takeaway, he said, is the need for workers who are tech-savvy, whether that means running automation or working alongside it. He talked about partnering with workforce development boards, community colleges and the Pre-K-12 system to get those changing skills into classrooms. Kern's unemployment has historically run above the state average, with agriculture's seasonality pushing joblessness up in winter and down in the growing months — so what happens to training pipelines here is not abstract.

**Bakersfield Now also reports that President Trump says the White House is exploring Trump Accounts for adults.** The accounts, as described, would be a new savings vehicle, and the administration says it is looking at extending the concept beyond children. Details are still thin, and we'll pass along specifics as they firm up.

**KGET 17 reports that power has been restored to homes following a PG&E outage in southwest Bakersfield.** Crews got the lights back on for affected customers. Outages are a familiar nuisance in that part of town, and it's worth noting when they're resolved cleanly.

## Something good

The Kern County Sheriff's Office is hosting a National Night Out event that includes trick-or-treating, bringing deputies and residents together for an evening of community connection — a good chance for kids to meet the people who patrol their neighborhoods, and for grown-ups to put faces to the badges.

And Honor Flight veterans got a warm welcome back in Bakersfield after a special trip. Whatever else is going on, that's the kind of homecoming this town does well.

## Coming up this week

The Bakersfield City Council meets twice today at City Hall — a regular session at 5:15 p.m. and a second meeting at 3:30 p.m. Also today, the Special Prop 47 Local Advisory Committee convenes at 1 p.m. If you've got opinions about how the city spends its dollars or how Proposition 47 funds are directed locally, these are the rooms to be in.

Tonight at 6, Kern County Veteran Service holds a workshop at its office on Golden State Avenue to walk veterans through the VA benefits that make homebuying easier. Realtors and a veteran couple who just bought their first home will lead the session, aimed at cutting through a financing process that can feel convoluted. A note on the flyer: it lists the date as Thursday, October 21, but the 21st falls on a Wednesday, which is when the workshop is actually happening.

The Fox Theater has a full slate this week. Switchfoot brings the Forever Now Tour with special guest Anberlin tonight. Henry Cho's Empty Nest Tour lands Friday, October 23. Saturday, October 24 brings two shows — Fred Armisen's "Comedy for Musicians But Everyone is Welcome" and BLADE RAVE. And Sunday, October 25, REZA presents Edge of Illusion. If you're planning further out, the Fox has also opened a season pass for its Cults & Classics series running through 2026 and 2027.

Have a good Wednesday, and stay dry out there.

top.title: New poll shows Becerra with wide lead over Hilton in California governor race
